PR surface: Source +1, Tests +25. Total +26 across 2 files.

target.title: fix(matrix): recognize MiniMax mm: namespaced reasoning tags in monitor replies
target.body:
Related: #89473

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users could see hidden MiniMax reasoning text in monitor replies when a model reply used `mm:` thinking tags such as `<mm:think>`, `<mm:thinking>`, or `<mm:thought>`.

Without this patch, Matrix could suppress replies that were entirely reasoning, but mixed reasoning-plus-visible replies could still deliver the hidden reasoning block into the room along with the visible answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Matrix now strips recognized thinking blocks before the Matrix send boundary, instead of only using them to decide whether a whole reply is reasoning-only.
- The stripping uses the public shared `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking` reasoning-tag sanitizer so literal `<mm:think>` or `<antml:think>` examples inside inline/fenced code are preserved without importing core private files from the Matrix package.
- The follow-up regression covers the waiting-on-author review request for mixed `mm:`/`antml:` reasoning blocks in text replies and locks the code-example preservation boundary.

## User Impact

Matrix users no longer receive hidden reasoning text when a monitor reply mixes visible answer text with MiniMax or Anthropic-style thinking blocks. Visible reply text still sends normally, and answers that discuss reasoning tags as literal code examples are not corrupted.

## Evidence

- Real Matrix room proof from the earlier synced head remains relevant for the original reasoning-only path: a disposable unencrypted Matrix room on matrix.org received exactly one visible Matrix event while three `mm:` reasoning-only replies were suppressed at the Matrix monitor delivery boundary.
- Additional mixed-path delivery-boundary proof on this head used the real `deliverMatrixReplies -> sendMessageMatrix -> client.sendMessage` Matrix send path with a fake Matrix client capturing final event content. It verified hidden `mm:` and `antml:` reasoning blocks were removed before outbound Matrix payloads, while a literal code example was preserved:

  ```text
  Matrix mixed reasoning delivery proof passed
  {
    "bodies": [
      "Visible answer",
      "Second answer",
      "Literal example: `<mm:think>draft</mm:think>`"
    ],
    "eventCount": 3
  }
  ```

- Focused Matrix regression test with the public SDK sanitizer import:

  ```text
  $ node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts
  [test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-matrix.config.ts
  The `envFile` option is deprecated, please use `envDir: false` instead.

   RUN  v4.1.9 [local path redacted]


   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  9 passed (9)
     Start at  22:00:17
     Duration  2.74s (transform 2.57s, setup 1.18s, import 817ms, tests 378ms, environment 0ms)

  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 15.60s
  ```

- Whitespace/conflict-marker check:

  ```text
  git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
  Validation result: pass, exit_code=0, 143ms
  ```

- Changed-file checks passed locally after refreshing dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` to avoid this host's `node-llama-cpp` postinstall/CMake 3.19 issue:

  ```text
  $ node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts
  [check:changed] lanes=extensions, extensionTests
  [check:changed] extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts: extension test
  [check:changed] extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts: extension production
  [check:changed] typecheck extensions
  [check:changed] typecheck extension tests
  [check:changed] runtime import cycles
  Import cycle check: 0 runtime value cycle(s).
  ```

- What was not rerun: an external Matrix homeserver room proof for the new mixed-block scenario. The previous disposable Matrix credentials and proof harness are not present in this workspace, so the new evidence is a local delivery-boundary run through the real Matrix send code with a fake client capturing the exact outbound event bodies.
